details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has introduced Pontes, a new service allowing eurozone banks to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets using central bank money. This initiative marks a significant step in the Eurosystem's strategy to integrate distributed ledger technology (DLT) into traditional finance, aiming to enhance the speed and efficiency of transactions and reduce reliance on private stablecoins for institutional settlements. The ECB also plans to invest in digital securities.
title: ECB Launches Pontes System for Tokenized Asset Settlement

details: The European Central Bank and other EU central banks are advocating against a Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation that mandates major stablecoin issuers to hold 60% of their reserves as bank deposits. They argue that this requirement could expose lenders to volatility in the stablecoin market and propose instead that a minimum percentage of reserves be held in assets maturing within one to five working days to enhance liquidity and stability.
title: ECB Opposes MiCA Rule on Stablecoin Bank Deposits

details: Bitcoin climbed above $81,000, recovering from earlier declines, as global financial markets demonstrated a renewed "risk-on" sentiment. This rally is attributed to positive exchange-traded fund (ETF) flows and an increased investor appetite for riskier assets, occurring despite recent Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and the stalled US crypto regulation bill. Smaller altcoins also experienced notable gains during this period.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $81,000 Amid Renewed Risk Appetite

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has completed a periodic review of its Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP), updating it to address the evolving financial landscape. The revised program will now feature an expanded focus on systemic and emerging risks, specifically including those related to nonbank financial institutions, artificial intelligence (AI), and crypto assets, acknowledging their increasing significance in global financial stability.
title: IMF Integrates Crypto Assets into Financial Stability Assessments

details: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) raised its benchmark interest rate to 1.25%, reaching its highest level in 31 years. This decision has significantly influenced the Japanese yen and is being closely monitored for its effects on yen carry trades. Although Bitcoin initially saw a modest increase, the tightening of Japanese monetary policy can elevate the cost of yen-funded positions, potentially exerting downward pressure on global risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Bank of Japan Rate Hike Impacts Yen Carry Trades and Crypto Markets
